description: A real Singapore Airlines boarding pass (MNL to SIN) returned no originAirport/destinationAirport, even though both codes are clearly printed. Both legs are printed the same way (code next to its own local time) -- this is not two different document layouts. The OCR's text-box detection just grouped the two legs inconsistently: "SIN" and "20:50" came back as one line ("SIN 20:50", needs the 0.9.0 code-near-time pattern), while "MNL" and "17:05" came back as two separate lines ("MNL" alone needs the 0.10.0 bare-code-line pattern). Each pattern ran as its own complete pass over the whole document and only ever found its one matching code -- the code-near-time pass found only SIN, the bare-code-line pass found only MNL -- so neither pass's "exactly two distinct codes" threshold was ever met, even though the two codes together were sitting right there. Fixed by checking both patterns per line and merging into one combined candidate list, which catches this regardless of which way OCR happened to split the two legs -- still bounded by the same "exactly two distinct codes, or don't guess" rule.
